subject: BonfyreFS/ObjectFabric semantic compaction: reclaim bytes by deduplication and proof-preserving relocation, not repeated leaf deletion

body.objective: Turn storage into a content-addressed semantic metabolism layer while disk is tight.
required_actions: Inventory active Run8 artifacts, receipts, replay fixtures, generated projections and historical evidence by content identity. Detect duplicate bytes and duplicate semantic payloads before deleting anything.

Where the registered BonfyreFS/ObjectFabric path exists, stream immutable artifacts into content-addressed storage with BLAKE3/SHA binding, compress homogeneous cold packs with Zstd when net-positive, and retain graph references plus recovery metadata.

Use OpenDAL as the storage boundary where already integrated; do not hard-code a second filesystem abstraction. Iroh/QUIC replication is eligible only if an existing configured path is available and authority permits it.
After exact readback/replay proof, delete redundant source copies and emit a batched/Merkle DeletionProof instead of thousands of tiny proof files.
Keep live epoch files, active envs, secrets, current source and unsatisfied evidence frontiers pinned. Semantic reachability, not filename age, decides liveness.

Measure dedup_ratio, compressed_ratio, proof_bytes, reclaimed_bytes, replay_success and regeneration_rate. If compaction writes more than it can reclaim under current free space, defer rather than self-OOM.
body.cross_graph_rule: ResourceGraph should prefer proof-preserving dedup/compaction before destructive rebuildable deletion when the semantic value per retained byte is higher.
